newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing - limited deficits needed for Euro.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing - limited deficits needed for Euro.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday that trust in Europe's new common currency, the Euro, could be secured only if the budget deficits of currency member nations were limited.

Noting policy makers could waste no time in convincing Europeans the currency will be stable, Issing said: "This can be reached if nations' budget deficits are reduced to a level which will not endanger the currency's stability."

"The strict interpretation of convergence criteria at the entry to a currency union and a pact to secure durable fiscal stability after the introduction of the Euro are therefore unavoidable," Issing said.
Issing was addressing a banking forum and a text of his speech was made available beforehand.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that there was some room for interpretation when evaluating whether states have met the Maastricht Treaty entry criteria.
